desc:
The Fibonacci sequence used here starts F1 = 1 and F2 = 1, and every later term is the sum of the two before it: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, ...

Given a positive integer n, return the smallest index k ≥ 1 such that Fk ≥ n.

n = 1       -> 1   (F1 = 1)
n = 2       -> 3   (F3 = 2)
n = 6       -> 6   (F5 = 5 is too small, F6 = 8)
n = 832040  -> 30  (F30 = 832040)
hints: Generate the Fibonacci numbers in order and count as you go until one is large enough.
Only about 45 terms are needed before the values pass 10<sup>9</sup>, so a plain loop is fast.
Keep the current term and the next term in two variables and advance both together.
editorial: Walk the sequence from the start. Keep a = Fk and b = Fk+1; while a is smaller than n, shift the pair one step forward and increase k. The first k at which a reaches n is the answer.
The terms grow exponentially, so the loop runs only about 45 times for n up to 10<sup>9</sup>. A binary search over precomputed terms would also work, but at this size it is not needed.
